answer: In the lagoon registry, an AI agent minting a key must submit a zk-SNARK proof of computing 10^14 sequential SHA-256 walnut hashes over a unique marble seed. This imposes an irreversible compute loss per key, not a temporary capital lockup. Because proofs bind to a single public key and resetting requires a fresh proof, spawning N fake identities scales linearly at 10^14 × N sequential operations.
